output.brief: The rejects come from an interaction. Arnholt resin arrives wetter than Quillan, and dryer D5 is degraded (dew point about −16 to −19 °C instead of −40 °C). Together they leave resin at the Press 5 throat at 0.25–0.31% moisture, above the 0.20% limit, which causes splay and latch cracks. Press 5 with Arnholt rejects about 10%. Press 5 with Quillan runs 0.9%. Press 7 with Arnholt runs 0.8%. A lot dried in a good portable dryer and run on Press 5 rejected 0.8%. The second-shift gap is only because all second-shift VX runs on Press 5. New and experienced operators perform the same, so the performance plans would punish the wrong people. Dropping Arnholt isn't needed. Maintenance's "dryers are fine" argument fails because Quillan resin tolerated the bad dryer and Arnholt does not. This week: repair D5 (heater and desiccant), restore the −15 alarm limit to its original setting, keep Arnholt off D5 until D5 is verified, and add a throat moisture check for every lot. Open question: Arnholt's wetter inlet resin may come from north-annex storage rather than the supplier. Every Arnholt sample came from the annex, so test that before paying for moving the stock. I'm fairly confident in the main finding.
